title: Compact sparkline sidecar switcher for rolled dashboards and cost lanes
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Goal: Prototype a compact sidecar 'sparkline' switcher that sits adjacent to the left rail and surfaces contextual micro-dashboards (rollout health, cost lanes, recent regressions) without forcing a full route change. The widget should support quick workspace switching, lightweight drill-in, and an expand-to-panel affordance for deeper workflows.

Why: Current console navigation demands full page transitions for telemetry-led checks (cost, latency, rollout status). Common user flows are: 1) glance at cost trends while inspecting a model route, 2) quickly toggle rollout canaries between two variants, 3) jump between workspaces when an alert originates from another team. These are high-frequency, low-attention tasks where heavyweight routing hurts velocity.

Success metrics: reduce average time-to-first-action for rollout triage by 35%, reduce route changes for cost-check flows by 50%, and achieve NPS + usability score >= 85 in a 10-user prototype study.

Design constraints and principles: compact (40–240px width depending on collapsed state), predictable keyboard navigation, clear visual separation from primary left rail, preserve left-rail accessibility semantics (aria-roles), no new top-level navigation entries (must be a contextual augmentation), respect tenant/per-project RBAC and hide controls that users lack permission for. Motion should be subtle; prefer cross-fades and slide-ins with reduced-motion support.

UX patterns explored:
- Inline sparkline strip: micro sparkline + metric chips + quick action (Pause rollout / Promote / Open drifts).
- Stacked microcards: small stacked panes for Rollouts / Costs / Errors with vertical swipe on touch.
- Expand-to-modal: CTA on a microcard expands to a medium panel that reuses the Console rollouts screen and preserves scroll position.

Decisions so far:
- Chosen pattern: Inline sparkline strip + single expand panel. It gives highest glanceability while enabling full tasks.
- Default collapsed state shows three chips: (Rollouts sparkline, Cost sparkline, Errors count). Hover reveals the inline controls; click opens the medium panel.
- Accessibility: Keyboard focus lands on the first chip; arrow keys cycle chips; Enter expands. All controls have aria-labels and live region updates when a rollout action completes.

Prototypes and artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/redwood/console-sidecar-sparkline-proto (frames: CompactStrip, ExpandedPanel, A11yFlow)
- Interactive prototype (InVision): https://invision.redwood.design/proto/sidecar-sparkline
- Requirements doc / PRD: Google Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/console-sidecar-prd
- Example dashboard query: BigQuery cost-sparkline SQL snippet attached in PRD.

Acceptance criteria:
- Visual comps for collapsed/hover/expanded states approved by PM and Design Lead.
- Prototype tested with 8–12 engineers/product owners with tasks covering glance, promote/cancel rollout, and workspace switch. Usability notes captured.
- Handoff tokens + component spec ready for engineering (CSS tokens, motion specs, aria roles).
- Spike completed by ENG to estimate backend telemetry endpoints and permissions gating (ENG-4821).

Next steps:
1) Iterate on microcopy for rollout quick actions (Riley to propose in comments).
2) Engineering spike (ENG-4821) to deliver API contract for quick action endpoints and streaming health updates.
3) Visual QA and dark-mode polish.
4) Schedule prototype usability sessions (UX research + 10 participants) and synthesize results into this ticket.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We avoid adding a persistent top-level nav entry to minimize IA churn; downside is discoverability — mitigated with a short on-boarding tooltip and one-week banner.
- Inline controls are intentionally limited to reduce risk of accidental destructive actions; full destructive flows route to expanded panel with confirmation.

Risks:
- RBAC complexity may increase number of API calls; we may need to cache permission checks per session.
- Potential conflicts with other left-rail experiments (coordinate with DES-903210 and DES-902468 owners).
